correctness.rationale: For exactly the twelve-vertex graph C6 square K2 with its 18 rim/rung edges and the ordinary (not perfect-only) matching complex, face enumeration gives 1,104 augmented faces with 1,18,117,336,420,192,20 by size. I independently constructed the face family from edge-disjoint endpoint masks and replayed the pivot-toggle matching: 546 augmented pairs, 12 residual four-edge faces; after removing the empty pair there is one critical 0-cell and twelve critical 3-cells. I independently oriented all 4,020 augmented Hasse incidences, checked a topological order of all 1,104 vertices (4,002 nonempty incidences), hence acyclicity. Forman then gives an integral wedge of twelve S3, not just Betti ranks. The inspected code computes signed fixed-matching reduced Lefschetz sums for all 24 graph automorphisms and exact rational D6 x C2 orthogonality; its character rows and multiplicities are consistent (total dimension 12, layer trace -2 -> 5/7 eigenspaces, trivial multiplicity one). The independent checker specifically confirms the topological premise; no universal prism assertion is inferred.

value.rationale: The nonouterplanar smallest even cyclic ladder after the cube has a natural ordinary matching complex with maximal nonperfect matchings; both its integral homotopy and the FULL D6 x C2 character are meaningful missing exact invariants, not just a finite count. The 5 versus 7 layer eigenspace split and the unique global invariant line cannot be recovered from a wedge multiplicity or the recently studied perfect-matching subcomplex. One explicit graph can be a useful symmetry benchmark without an all-ladder theorem.
